l4_steps.name: Scan unserved O&D opportunities
l4_steps.input: Historical booking data, MIDT traffic feeds, interline itinerary reports
l4_steps.output: Long list of candidate unserved or underserved city pairs
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum 20 candidate markets identified per planning cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: MIDT data excludes LCC-direct bookings, leading to demand underestimation in price-sensitive leisure markets

l4_steps.name: Benchmark competitor schedules on candidates
l4_steps.output: Competitor capacity, frequency, and fare level summary per market
l4_steps.kpi: Competitive gap identified for ≥60% of shortlisted markets
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG data lags real-time charter and codeshare capacity additions by up to 3 weeks

l4_steps.name: Screen markets against minimum demand threshold
l4_steps.input: O&D traffic volumes and OAG competitor data
l4_steps.output: Shortlisted markets with ≥150 unserved or recapturable pax/day
l4_steps.kpi: Demand threshold screening accuracy ≥90% vs. post-launch actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: Redshift demand cubes are refreshed weekly; intra-week traffic spikes from events or promotions not captured

l4_steps.name: Forecast 12-month O&D demand per market
l4_steps.input: Shortlisted markets, seasonality curves, macro-economic indices
l4_steps.output: Monthly O&D demand forecast with P10/P50/P90 confidence bands
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST models calibrated on existing network may not reflect latent demand in markets with no prior service

l4_steps.name: Simulate network spill and recapture impact
l4_steps.input: Demand forecast, existing schedule SSIM file
l4_steps.output: Incremental revenue estimate, spill/recapture matrix, connecting feed impact
l4_steps.kpi: Spill recapture rate ≥35% for new route
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM simulations assume fixed itinerary preference weights; actual passenger path choice in new markets is untested

l4_steps.name: Model yield and price elasticity
l4_steps.input: Demand forecast, competitor fare benchmarks from OAG
l4_steps.output: Projected RASM, average fare, and fare class mix by month
l4_steps.kpi: Projected RASM ≥ CASM + 15% margin at base-case load factor of 83%
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM fare elasticity models trained on existing markets; new leisure markets may exhibit steeper price sensitivity than modelled

l4_steps.name: Produce consolidated revenue forecast report
l4_steps.input: RASM/CASM output from NRM and SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Revenue forecast dashboard and market scorecard
l4_steps.kpi: Scorecard completed within 2 business days of demand model sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual data collation from SkyCAST, SkySYM, and NRM increases error risk and delays review cycle

l4_steps.name: Optimise fleet assignment for candidate route
l4_steps.input: Proposed frequency and timing, existing fleet utilisation plan
l4_steps.output: Optimal aircraft gauge and rotation plan for new route
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyMAX optimisation can downgrade candidate route gauge when existing network utilisation is near ceiling, creating circular infeasibility

l4_steps.name: Evaluate frequency and timing trade-offs
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment output, competitive departure timing benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Recommended departure times and frequency options (1x, 2x, 3x daily)
l4_steps.kpi: Scheduling conflict rate <5% in SkyWORKS validation
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyWORKS turnaround time constraints at congested focus-city stations (e.g. LAS, MDW) restrict viable departure windows to <3 options

l4_steps.name: Confirm spare aircraft availability at launch date
l4_steps.input: Proposed launch date, fleet delivery schedule, maintenance forecast
l4_steps.output: Aircraft availability confirmation or gap identification
l4_steps.kpi: Spare cover ratio ≥5% of active fleet on launch date
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing 737 MAX delivery delays (post-FAA recertification cycle) have repeatedly compressed launch windows by 6–18 months

l4_steps.name: Check slot availability at origin and destination
l4_steps.input: Proposed departure times, airport coordination level (L1/L2/L3)
l4_steps.output: Slot availability status, coordination response, or waiver requirement
l4_steps.kpi: Preferred slot obtained within ±30 min of target for ≥80% of requests
l4_steps.pain_point: Slot-coordinated airports (Level 3) at international gateways impose 6–12 month lead times; historical precedence rules favour incumbents over new entrants

l4_steps.name: Validate gate and ground handling feasibility
l4_steps.input: Proposed departure and arrival times, station gate inventory
l4_steps.output: Gate assignment feasibility report and required turnaround buffer
l4_steps.kpi: Gate conflict rate <2% for new route insertion
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS data quality at smaller domestic stations is often incomplete; manual verification with airport authority adds 1–2 weeks

l4_steps.name: Assess crew pairing efficiency for new route
l4_steps.input: Proposed schedule, crew base locations, FAR Part 117 duty limits
l4_steps.output: Crew pairing cost estimate and minimum crew headcount requirement
l4_steps.kpi: Crew cost per block hour for new route ≤ system average + 10%
l4_steps.pain_point: Routes originating from non-crew-base stations require deadhead positioning, adding $800–$1,200/day per crew pair and inflating CASM

l4_steps.name: Build full-route P&L model
l4_steps.input: RASM forecast, CASM drivers, crew cost estimate, airport fees
l4_steps.output: 12-month route P&L with EBIT, ROIC, and contribution margin
l4_steps.kpi: ROIC ≥12% in base-case scenario at month 12
l4_steps.pain_point: Airport fee structures at new international destinations often require renegotiation; provisional estimates in SAP can overstate profitability by 8–15%

l4_steps.name: Run sensitivity and break-even load factor analysis
l4_steps.input: P&L model, P10/P50/P90 demand scenarios from SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Break-even load factor, downside ROIC, and go/no-go recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Break-even load factor ≤75%; downside P10 ROIC ≥6%
l4_steps.pain_point: Sensitivity model inputs (fuel price, FX, competitor response) are manually refreshed quarterly; stale assumptions distort go/no-go threshold

l4_steps.name: Compile and submit commercial committee pack
l4_steps.input: Business case deck, P&L model, ops feasibility sign-off, demand forecast
l4_steps.output: Formal new market entry proposal submitted to Commercial Committee
l4_steps.kpi: Pack submission ≥10 business days before committee review date
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-functional sign-off (Revenue Mgmt, Ops, Finance) often delayed due to differing planning horizons; average pack completion takes 18 days vs. 10-day target

l4_steps.name: File approved schedule and slots in SkyWORKS
l4_steps.input: Commercial Committee approval, proposed SSIM schedule record
l4_steps.output: New market schedule inserted into official season file
l4_steps.kpi: Schedule filed ≥120 days before service start (IATA SSIM standard)
l4_steps.pain_point: Late approvals compress the SSIM filing window, risking GDS distribution gaps and reducing advance booking lead time below optimal 90-day curve

l4_steps.name: Publish new route to GDS and NDC channels
l4_steps.input: Approved SSIM schedule, fare filing from ATPCO
l4_steps.output: New route live in Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, Amadeus GDS, and NDC channel
l4_steps.kpi: GDS content live ≥90 days before first departure; NDC content live within 24 hours of GDS
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare filing cycle runs twice daily; missed filing window delays public fare availability by up to 12 hours, impacting early adopter bookings on launch-day announcement
